items.title: Three Ways Each Link Conditions the Next: Present, Immediate, and Long-Delayed

items.zh: 問：無明與行為作俱有緣？為作無間滅緣？為作久遠滅緣？答：當知具作三緣。謂由無知，於隨順諸行法中，為俱有覆障緣，為彼彼事發起諸行。又由惡見、放逸俱行無知，為無間滅生起緣，發起諸行。又由無知，為久遠滅引發緣故，建立順彼當生相續。
items.en: Question: Does ignorance serve as a co-present condition for formations, an immediately-preceding condition, or a long-delayed condition? Answer: It should be understood that ignorance provides all three. Through simple not-knowing, it serves as a co-present, obstructing condition amid the things that lead one into formations, prompting formations for this or that particular purpose. Further, through not-knowing bound up with wrong views and heedlessness, it serves as the immediately-preceding condition that triggers formations' actual arising. Further, through not-knowing, it serves as a long-delayed, inducing condition, establishing the continuity of the coming life that accords with it.

items.zh: 問：云何應知諸行望識為三種緣？答：由能熏發彼種子故，為俱有緣。次後由彼勢力轉故，為無間滅生起緣。由彼當來果得生故，為久遠滅引發緣。如行望識，如是識望名色、名色望六處、六處望觸、觸望受亦爾。問：云何應知受望愛為三種緣？答：當知由彼起樂著故，為俱有緣。從此無間，由彼勢力起追求等作用轉故，為無間滅生起緣。建立當來難可解脫彼相續故，為久遠滅引發緣。問：云何愛望取為三種緣？答：由欲貪俱行，於隨順取法中，欲樂安立故，為俱有緣。由無間滅勢力轉故，為生起緣。建立當來難可解脫彼相續故，為久遠滅引發緣。問：云何取望有為三種緣？答：由與彼俱，令業能招諸趣果故，為俱有緣。又由彼力，於此生處能引識等故，為無間滅生起緣。又能引發彼界功能故，為久遠滅引發緣。問：云何有望生為三種緣？答：熏發彼種子故，為俱有緣。由彼勢力無間隨轉故，為生起緣。雖久遠滅而果轉故，為引發緣。如有望生，當知生望老死為緣亦爾。復次，建立有支有二種：一、就勝分建立，謂取所攝受業，如前已說。二、全分建立，謂業及識乃至受所有種子，取所攝受，建立為有應知。問：是諸有支唯有次第與行為緣乃至老死，更有餘業用耶？答：即此業用，及於各別所行境中，如其所應所有業用，當知是名第二業用。問：無明唯與行為緣，亦與餘支為緣耶？答：無明乃至亦與老死為緣。前言唯與行為緣者，但說近緣義。如是所餘盡應當知。

items.title: Why Practice Always Cuts the Chain Backward, Never Forward

items.zh: 復次，後支非前支緣。何以故？如為斷後支故，勤作功用斷於前支，由前斷故，後亦隨斷。非為斷前故，勤作功用斷於後支。是故當知唯此為彼緣。
items.en: Further, a later link is never a condition for an earlier one. Why is this so? One who wishes to end a later link applies effort to end the earlier one, and because the earlier link is ended, the later link ends as well, following of its own accord. One never applies effort to end a later link for the sake of ending an earlier one. It should therefore be understood: only the earlier serves as condition for the later, never the reverse.

items.zh: 問：云何說言此有故彼有？答：由未斷緣，餘得生義故。問：云何此生故彼生？答：由無常緣，餘得生義故。問：何故說言有生故有老死，要由生緣而有老死，如是乃至無明望行？答：由此言教道理，顯從無實作用緣，餘得生義故。問：何故說言有生故有老死，非離生緣而有老死，如是乃至無明望行？答：由此言教道理，顯從自相續緣；即自相續，餘得生義故。
items.en: Question: What is meant by saying "this existing, that comes to exist"? Answer: Because, so long as a condition remains unsevered, a further thing is thereby able to arise. Question: What is meant by "this arising, that arises"? Answer: Because it is precisely through an impermanent condition that a further thing is able to arise.

items.title: A Four-Cornered Test: Is Every Case of the Condition Also a Case of the Result?

items.zh: 問：若法無明為緣，彼法是行耶？設是行者，彼無明為緣耶？答：應作四句。或有行非無明為緣，謂無漏及無覆無記身語意行。或無明為緣而非是行，謂除行所攝有支所餘有支。或有亦無明為緣亦是行，謂福、非福、不動身語意行。除如是相，是第四句。
items.en: Question: If a thing is conditioned by ignorance, is it necessarily formations? And if it is formations, is it necessarily conditioned by ignorance? Answer: Four cases should be made. There is formations not conditioned by ignorance — namely, uncontaminated bodily, verbal, and mental activity, and unobscured, morally neutral activity. There is what is conditioned by ignorance yet is not formations — namely, every link other than formations. There is what is both conditioned by ignorance and is formations — namely, meritorious, demeritorious, and unmoving bodily, verbal, and mental activity. And apart from these three, there is a fourth case — neither conditioned by ignorance nor formations at all, belonging to none of the twelve links.

items.zh: 問：若行為緣，彼亦識耶？設是識者，行為緣耶？答：應作四句。或行為緣非識，謂除識所餘有支。或識非行為緣，謂無漏識及無覆無記識，除異熟生。或亦識亦行為緣，謂後有種子識及果識。除如是相，是第四句。由此道理，乃至觸緣受，隨其所應四句應知。
items.en: Question: If a thing is conditioned by formations, is it necessarily consciousness? And if it is consciousness, is it necessarily conditioned by formations? Answer: Four cases should be made. There is what is conditioned by formations yet is not consciousness — every link other than consciousness. There is consciousness not conditioned by formations — uncontaminated consciousness, and unobscured, morally neutral consciousness, excepting what is born of ripening. There is what is both consciousness and conditioned by formations — the seed-consciousness of a further existence, and its resulting consciousness. And, apart from these, a fourth case belonging to none of the twelve links. By this same reasoning, the four cases for every remaining pair, down through contact conditioning feeling, should be understood accordingly.

blocks.text: A short but important passage. It explains how each link conditions the next in three different time-frames, and then states a principle with direct consequences for practice: to end a later link, one must end an earlier one. The chain is always cut backwards.
Each link can condition the next in three ways:

items: **co-present** (俱有): at the same time, as ignorance accompanies and obstructs the formation it drives;
**immediately preceding** (無間): in the very next moment, as ignorance with wrong view and heedlessness leads straight into action;
**long-delayed** (久遠): after a long interval. Master Cháng Bǎi: "Though past deeds long ago ceased, the seeds they imprinted arise when the conditions for birth come, producing results."

blocks.text: Ignorance provides all three to formations. The third is the one that makes karma across lives intelligible: a deed's seed can wait for eons (Day 7) and then condition a new life.

"A later link never conditions an earlier one." And so: "One who wishes to end a later link applies effort to end the earlier one, and because the earlier link is ended, the later link ends as well … One never ends an earlier link by ending a later one."

This has a plain meaning for practice. We cannot remove ageing and death by working on ageing and death. We cannot remove suffering by working on feeling itself; feeling is a result. We work where the causes are: on craving and grasping, which we can catch in the moment (Day 18's "feeling is the basis from which craving arises"), and finally on ignorance, through insight.

"This arising, that arises" means arising through an impermanent condition. Venerable Miào Jìng: "things that arise and cease condition things that arise and cease, not the unarising-unceasing." Master Cháng Bǎi: this again rules out a permanent creator as a cause (Day 47).

The treatise then tests each pair of links with a four-cornered analysis (四句): is every case of the earlier link also a case of the later, or vice versa, or both, or neither? For example, is every ignorance followed by formations? Not when the ignorance is of a kind that produces no karma. The point of the exercise is precision: the formula "A conditions B" is not mechanical; each pair has its own conditions and exceptions.
The next passage takes up one exception that matters to every practitioner: a longing that looks like craving but is not.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, which kind of condition does ignorance provide for formations?
options: all three — co-present, immediately-preceding, and long-delayed
quiz.why: "It should be understood that ignorance provides all three": co-present and obstructing, immediately-preceding with wrong view and heedlessness, and long-delayed inducing. Venerable Miào Jìng: they resemble results now, next life, and later — the co-present one is like a present-life result.

quiz.q: What is the "long-delayed inducing condition," according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: though past deeds have long ceased, the seeds they planted arise and bear fruit when conditions meet
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Though past deeds long ago ceased, the seeds they imprinted arise when birth-conditions come, producing results." The text: ignorance "establishes the continuity that will give rise to" a future life — the lecture reads this as the future body, not a future formation.

quiz.q: The treatise says a later link never conditions an earlier one. Why?
options: to end a later link one ends the earlier, and the later follows; one never ends a later link to end an earlier one
quiz.why: "One who wishes to end a later link applies effort to end the earlier one, and because the earlier link is ended, the later link ends as well … One never applies effort to end a later link for the sake of ending an earlier one." Master Cháng Bǎi: to end formations, end ignorance.

quiz.q: "This arising, that arises" means arising through an impermanent condition. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say this rules out?
options: conditioned things cause conditioned things; the unconditioned cannot cause arising
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Things that arise and cease condition things that arise and cease — not the unarising-unceasing." Master Cháng Bǎi: this refutes the Mahāsāṃghika view that the unconditioned produces conditioned things, and non-Buddhist eternalism.
